title: GradingVerdict
description: One reader's answer to one task — exactly one CURRENT row per (task, reader). A re-save replaces the row and bumps `version` (previous versions are retained server-side for audit and are not surfaced in v1). The six-verdict vocabulary is SPEC-confirmation-run.md §6.6.2's, byte-for-byte what `s0_rdev_score.py` accepts; the per-span judgements are the pilot sheet's question (a) — *is each supplied span correctly located and minimal?* — and the pair-level `verdict` is the reader's answer to (a) and (b) together.

reader.description: The resolved subject of the reader who saved this row — always the caller on a PUT.

verdict.description: `correct`: every supplied span is correctly located and minimal, and nothing material was missed. `wrong-location`: a supplied span's quote is real but that location does not justify relevance (incl. the deep-section trap). `non-minimal`: a supplied set contains a span that could be deleted without losing sufficiency. `missed-evidence`: there is evidence in this document the labeler did not supply (applies to positives and negatives alike). `correctly-none`: the labeler supplied nothing and the reader agrees. `ambiguous`: the reader cannot decide whether this is one unit or two, or whether a span is sufficient — neutral, adjudicated later.

span_judgements.description: Question (a), per span. Each entry names a span of the task by (`set`, `span`) — `set` is an evidence set's `set_index`, `span` the 1-based position in that set's `spans`; the pilot sheet's `<set>.<span>` key split in two. A judgement naming a span the task does not have is a 422. Empty when the task has no claims.

extra_answers.description: Answers to the task's `extra_questions`, keyed by their `id`. An unknown id, or a non-`yes`/`no` answer to a `yes-no` question, is a 422. Empty when the task has none.

notes.description: Free text: what the reader looked at, what was missing, why ambiguous. Exported verbatim as the CSV `notes` column. Empty string when none.

version.description: 1 on the first save for this (task, reader); +1 on every re-save. Strictly monotonic; a client that shows `Recorded …, change it and save again` can compare versions to detect a stale view.

saved_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of this version.

set.description: An evidence set's `set_index` on the task (1-based).

span.description: 1-based position of the span within that set's `spans`.

judgement.description: `located`: correctly located and minimal. `wrong`: wrong location. `non-minimal`: not minimal.

answer.description: `yes` or `no` for a `yes-no` question; any string for a `text` question.
